question.leadin: These men got the idea of flying from the bicycle shop they worked at.
question.text: Name these brothers, who invented the first airplane and successfully had a test flight near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
question.clue: With Glenn Curtiss, this group established a corporation that still exists today, which is headquartered in North Carolina.

swap.text: Created in response to the Supreme Court case of Pollock vs. Farmer's Loan and Trust, this amendment created the federal income tax.
swap.clue: It was introduced by Sereno Payne in order to fulfill a debate promise, and when it unexpectedly passed the Senate, Payne began lobbying against its ratification.

question.text: The Atlanta Compromise was criticized as weak by W.E.B. Du Bois and other co-founders of this American civil rights organization. Thurgood Marshall represented this group in arguments before the Supreme Court, including Brown v. Board.
question.answerHtml: NAACP (accept National Association for the Advancement of Colored People)
question.clue: Ralph David Abernathy was first part of this group before he led the SCLC.

swap.leadin: This event was fictionalized in Inherit the Wind.
swap.text: Name this event in which a Tennessee school teacher was accused of violating the Butler Act. During this trial, Clarence Darrow argued that the Butler Act was unconstitutional
swap.answerHtml: The Scopes Monkey trial (accept The State of Tennessee vs John Thomas Scopes)
swap.clue: Broadcast over WGN Radio, it addressed a violation of the Butler Act and was presided over by John Raulston.

question.leadin: The first of this man's namesake raids occurred on the second anniversary of the Bolshevik revolution.
question.text: Name this attorney general under Woodrow Wilson whose house was targeted by an anarchist bomb in 1919.
question.clue: Acting Secretary of Labor Louis Post undid many of this man's actions, which included a crackdown on the Union of Russian Workers for producing an anarchist manifesto.

swap.text: Noriega's predecessor, Omar Torrijos, signed two treaties with the United States to transfer control of this Atlantic-to-Pacific waterway back to Panama.
swap.clue: The Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty provided a strip of land twenty miles wide for this structure, whose construction was supervised by George Washington Goethals.

question.text: Later, as governor of Pennsylvania, Pinchot supported and helped implement this policy. The Volstead Act enacted this policy.
question.clue: Frances Willard advocated for this policy by creating the WCTU.

swap.text: Taft tried running for re-election, but the concurrent run of Theodore Roosevelt under this personal party named for an animal allowed Woodrow Wilson to come out on top.
swap.clue: Perhaps the greatest electoral successes of a party by this name came earlier, in California, where Hiram Johnson was elected governor and then Senator on its banner.

question.leadin: This writer's father Franklin became the first person to manufacture wooden oil tanks.
question.text: Name this writer who wrote a 19 part book on the company that eventually put Franklin out of business, often called the inventor of investigative journalism.
question.clue: In 1904, this muckraking journalist wrote The History of Standard Oil Company, detailing the company's abusive practices as part of a series of articles for McClure's Magazine.

swap.leadin: Name these "amendments" governing the Latin American policy of the U.S.
swap.text: This law, named for the Connecticut senator who put it forth on behalf of Secretary of State Root, permitted an exclusive U.S. right to intervene in Cuba.
swap.clue: This legislation prohibited a certain entity from entering into debt that it could not pay, or from making territorial concessions to anybody except the United States.

question.leadin: Former Milwaukee mayor Frank Zeidler was a member of this party, and helped to found its successor party in 1973.
question.text: Name this political party, led for a long time by Norman Thomas, which nominated Upton Sinclair in the 1926 California gubernatorial race.
question.clue: Victor Berger, a mayor of Milwaukee from this party, promoted a "sewer" variant of its namesake ideology.

swap.leadin: McClure's Magazine patronized many of the writers described by this epithet.
swap.text: Teddy Roosevelt provided what term for journalists who exposed the predations of large corporations around the turn of the 20th century?
swap.clue: This term was used to describe Henry Demarest Lloyd, the author of Wealth Against Commowealth, which critiqued an organization that was also exposed by Ida Tarbell.

question.text: This railroad trust that combined the companies of E.H. Harriman and James Hill was targeted by Theodore Roosevelt and declared unconstitutional in a namesake 1904 Supreme Court case.
question.answerHtml: Northern Securities Company [accept Northern Securities Company v. U.S.]
question.clue: Following the bankruptcy of the Northern Pacific Railway, J.P. Morgan formed this company to consolidate Midwestern railroads before it was declared a monopoly in a 1904 Supreme Court case.

swap.leadin: This act was drafted by Wayne Wheeler and named after the Chairman of the House Judiciary Committee.
swap.text: Name this Act that prohibited the production, transport, and sale of a certain class of substances, but did not explicitly prohibit their consumption.
swap.answerHtml: Volstead Act [prompt on National Prohibition Act; do not accept or prompt on “prohibition” or “Eighteenth Amendment”]
swap.clue: It was sponsored by the chair of the House Judiciary Committee, a congressman from Minnesota, and it gave power of enforcement to the Commissioner of Internal Revenue.

question.text: In 1910, Du Bois became the first editor of this official magazine of the NAACP. Jessie Redmon Fauset promoted the Harlem Renaissance as literary editor for this magazine.
question.clue: It begins by noting that the "summer soldier" and the "sunshine patriot" will shrink from facing the title challenge, in which "these are the times that try men's souls."

swap.text: This governor of Wyoming was the first woman to serve as a governor in the United States. This politician later served as the first female Director of the United States Mint.
swap.answerHtml: Nellie Tayloe Ross [or Nellie Davis Tayloe Ross; or Nellie Davis Tayloe]
swap.clue: This politician who successfully ran to be the first female governor in US history to finish out her husband's term. This politician narrowly lost the governor's seat to Frank Emerson in 1926.

question.text: The Pollock case resulted in the eventual passage and ratification of this law, which according to chief proponent Nebraska Senator Norris Brown "cannot be interpreted in two ways." It legalized the income tax.
question.clue: It became necessary after the Court's ruling in Pollock v. Farmer's Loan and Trust Company, even though the Court had earlier allowed a three percent levy to help finance the Civil War.

swap.leadin: In a series of interviews, this politician contrasted "honest graft" with "dishonest graft."
swap.text: Name this New York City political boss, the subject of a book subtitled "a series of very plain talks on very practical politics" written by William Riordan.

question.text: The earlier planned suburb of Coral Gables, Florida was developed entirely under the principles of this turn-of-the-century American urban planning philosophy that arose contemporaneously with the Garden City movement and inspired the McMillan Plan for redesigning Washington D.C.

swap.leadin: Name these figures associated with the Republic of Texas FTPE.
swap.text: This native Kentuckian served as aide-de-camp to Sam Houston during the war of independence, and then was named Texas's Secretary of War by Mirabeau Lamar. The leader of Confederate forces in the West, he was killed at the battle of Shiloh.
swap.clue: This congressman used the data of the 1890 census to set the quotas for new immigrants in the Immigrant Act of 1924, which he co-sponsored and names with Senator David Reed.
